root_cause.text: The amdxdna AIE2 mailbox management code allowed aie2_send_mgmt_msg_wait() to free and NULL out ndev->mgmt_chann on a timeout/error path, but other lifecycle paths such as aie2_hw_stop() later unconditionally used the same pointer without checking whether it had already been cleared.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message state “mgmt_chann may be set to NULL if the firmware returns an unexpected error in aie2_send_mgmt_msg_wait()” and that this “can later lead to a NULL pointer dereference in aie2_hw_stop()”; the patch adds aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann() with `if (!ndev->mgmt_chann) return;` and replaces direct `xdna_mailbox_stop_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann); xdna_mailbox_destroy_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann);` calls in aie2_hw_stop() and error paths.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE and commit message state “mgmt_chann may be set to NULL if the firmware returns an unexpected error in aie2_send_mgmt_msg_wait()” and that this “can later lead to a NULL pointer dereference in aie2_hw_stop()”; the patch adds aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann() with `if (!ndev->mgmt_chann) return;` and replaces direct `xdna_mailbox_stop_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann); xdna_mailbox_destroy_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann);` calls in aie2_hw_stop() and error paths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace open-coded management channel timeout cleanup with a dedicated destroy helper for centralized teardown logic.
intent_record.what: The timeout handling in aie2_send_mgmt_msg_wait() was changed from inlining three cleanup operations—calling xdna_mailbox_stop_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann), xdna_mailbox_destroy_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann), and setting ndev->mgmt_chann to NULL—to instead call the single helper aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann(ndev) when ret == -ETIME.
intent_record.how: At runtime, management-channel cleanup on timeout still occurs, but it is now delegated to a centralized helper, which ensures the destruction logic is performed through one shared path and can consistently handle channel teardown and state reset.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a safe management-channel teardown helper that stops and destroys the channel under the device lock and clears the pointer afterward.
intent_record.what: A new function `aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann(struct amdxdna_dev_hdl *ndev)` was added. It retrieves `xdna` from `ndev`, warns if `xdna->dev_lock` is not held, returns early if `ndev->mgmt_chann` is NULL, otherwise stops the mailbox channel, destroys it, and sets `ndev->mgmt_chann` to NULL.
intent_record.how: This adds an explicit teardown path for the management channel, ensuring the channel is only destroyed when it exists, is shut down in order before destruction, and the stored pointer is cleared afterward to prevent stale references or repeated destruction. The lock-state warning also helps catch incorrect call contexts during runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor management channel teardown in aie2_hw_stop() to use the shared aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann() helper.
intent_record.what: The code replaces three explicit management channel cleanup statements in aie2_hw_stop()—stopping the mailbox channel, destroying it, and setting ndev->mgmt_chann to NULL—with a single call to aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann(ndev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, management channel teardown is now performed through the helper function instead of open-coded steps in this function, centralizing the cleanup sequence and relying on the helper to handle stopping, destruction, and state reset for ndev->mgmt_chann.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace open-coded management channel teardown in the startup error path with the common aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann() helper.
intent_record.what: The error-handling block at the destroy_mgmt_chann label was changed from two direct calls, xdna_mailbox_stop_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann) and xdna_mailbox_destroy_channel(ndev->mgmt_chann), to a single wrapper call: aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann(ndev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, cleanup of the management channel on this failure path is now delegated to a dedicated helper instead of being open-coded locally, which centralizes the teardown behavior and may ensure any additional channel cleanup logic in the helper is consistently applied.

intent_record.intent_summary: Export the AIE2 management-channel destroy function so other code can trigger management-channel cleanup.
intent_record.what: A new function declaration, `void aie2_destroy_mgmt_chann(struct amdxdna_dev_hdl *ndev);`, was added to the `aie2_message.c` interface alongside the existing AIE2 message management function prototypes.
intent_record.how: This exposes a management-channel destruction routine to other translation units, enabling code outside `aie2_message.c` to invoke cleanup of the AIE2 management channel at runtime.

Exporting the AIE2 management-channel destroy function enables other lifecycle paths to perform the same management-channel cleanup involved in the bug, directly relating to the pointer free/clear handling around ndev->mgmt_chann.
